source: vampire.dll trace-mask immediates, as walked in docs/vtmb/navigation-jump-links.md
comment: The four questions a brush answers, and the retail mask that asks each. A brush's SIGNATURE
is its four answers; nothing downstream of the bake tests a contents bit again.
Only the BRUSH bits of each mask are kept: the entity bits (MONSTER 0x2000000) select which
entities a trace hits and are answered by those entities' own collision, not by world geometry.
The sight row is therefore 0x804091, the brush half of the game's one sight mask 0x2804091.

masks.question: does this brush block the player
does this brush block an NPC
note: The graph-build mask 0x2000b and the motor's 0x202400b differ from this one only in bits
no BRUSH carries differently: 0x2000b drops MOVEABLE (which is why links run through
standing doors) and 0x202400b adds MONSTER (an entity bit). All three carry MONSTERCLIP,
so one brush answer serves the build, the node fit and the motor alike.

masks.question: does this brush block sight
note: Carries neither WINDOW nor GRATE: an NPC sees through glass and grating.
SLIME 0x10 is on no brush of any shipped map, so it never decides an answer.
OPAQUE without SOLID is a light-blocker that still stops sight: 1,764 brushes on 25 maps.

masks.question: is this brush a pedestrian volume
note: Troika's own bit, tools/toolspedclip. The tie of %compilewanderclip to 0x2000 is an
inference by elimination and by name: clip brushes reach the BSP with their sides'
texinfo stripped, so no texture survives to witness it.
Only a brush carrying NO clip bit prices a route -- one that also carries MONSTERCLIP
stops InitLinks' own walk test, so no ground link is built across it to price.

comment: Retail's AI navigation has NO slope term of its own. CAI_MoveProbe_TestGroundMove
(0x102e4f50) clamps only on step height -- max(hullHeight * 0.5, StepHeight + 0.1) at
0x102e565b -- and CAI_MoveProbe_CheckStandPosition (0x102e7270) accepts a downward hull
trace iff it hit at all and the hit ENTITY's slot 164 allows standing; neither reads a
surface normal. An authored node graph needs no slope limit; a rasterised NavMesh does.
The port therefore takes retail's own standable normal from the player movement layer,
where the same world is stood on: 0.7 at 0x104492d0, already ported as
retail constant, not a tuning choice, but its application to NPC navigation is named.
